title: rorca-reasoning-engine

userStories.title: ReasoningCapability schema and type definitions
userStories.description: Define the ReasoningCapability TypeScript interface and all related types that will be shared across backend and frontend. This is the foundational schema that all other reasoning engine stories depend on.
acceptanceCriteria: ReasoningCapability interface exported from a shared types file with all fields: supportsReasoning, reasoningType, effortLevels, defaultEffort, budgetTokensSupported, budgetRange, costMultiplier
reasoningType is a discriminated union: 'anthropic-thinking' | 'effort-levels' | 'native-cot' | 'none'
ChatOptions.reasoning field added as optional: { enabled: boolean, effort?: string, budgetTokens?: number }
Spec JSON type updated to include optional reasoning field: { enabled: boolean, effort?: string }
npx tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors on both frontend and backend

userStories.title: ReasoningCapabilityDetector — algorithmic detection core
userStories.description: Build the ReasoningCapabilityDetector class in backend/src/lib/reasoning-detector.ts that algorithmically computes ReasoningCapability for any model ID without hardcoded lists. Supports Anthropic, OpenAI, and pattern-based detection.
acceptanceCriteria: detectCapability(modelId: string, metadata?: OpenRouterModelMetadata): ReasoningCapability function exported from reasoning-detector.ts
Claude 4.x models (matching claude-*-4-* pattern) return reasoningType: 'anthropic-thinking' with budgetTokensSupported: true and budgetRange: { min: 1024, max: 65536 }
OpenAI models starting with 'o' followed by a digit (o3, o4, o4-mini) return reasoningType: 'effort-levels' with effortLevels: ['low', 'medium', 'high']
Model IDs containing 'think', 'r1', 'qwq', 'reasoning' return reasoningType: 'native-cot'
Unknown models with no pattern match return { supportsReasoning: false, reasoningType: 'none' } without throwing
Jest unit tests cover all four detection paths with at least 3 model ID examples each

userStories.title: OpenRouter metadata reasoning detection
userStories.description: Extend ReasoningCapabilityDetector to parse OpenRouter model metadata (supported_parameters array, architecture fields) when available, and integrate with fetchOpenRouterModels() to attach reasoningCapability to every returned model.
acceptanceCriteria: detectCapability() accepts optional OpenRouterModelMetadata and checks supported_parameters array for 'reasoning', 'thinking', 'reasoning_effort' strings
When OpenRouter metadata is unavailable or malformed, falls back to ID-pattern matching without throwing
fetchOpenRouterModels() in config.ts attaches reasoningCapability to each model object using detectCapability(model.id, model)
GET /api/config/openrouter-models response includes reasoningCapability per model entry
Jest test mocks OpenRouter API response with a model having supported_parameters: ['reasoning'] and asserts supportsReasoning: true

userStories.title: Provider-agnostic reasoning mapping in llm-client.ts
userStories.description: Extend chatComplete() to translate the provider-agnostic ChatOptions.reasoning field into each provider's native format: Anthropic thinking blocks, OpenAI reasoning_effort, OpenRouter reasoning param. Remove the hardcoded GLM-5 reasoning logic.
acceptanceCriteria: Anthropic provider maps reasoning.enabled=true to thinking: { type: 'enabled', budget_tokens: budgetTokens ?? effort-mapped value } where effort 'low'→4096, 'medium'→16384, 'high'→32768
OpenAI provider maps reasoning.effort to reasoning_effort parameter in the request body when model is reasoning-capable
OpenRouter provider maps reasoning to { reasoning: { effort } } in request body
The hardcoded GLM-5 reasoning: { effort: 'high' } block is removed — replaced by the generic reasoning pass-through
When reasoning.enabled is false or reasoning is undefined, no reasoning params are sent to any provider
Integration test with mocked provider responses asserts correct native param shape for each provider

userStories.title: Claude CLI reasoning pass-through in execution-engine.ts
userStories.description: Extend spawnClaude() in execution-engine.ts to pass reasoning config as CLI flags. Add --reasoning-effort to the arg pipeline from worker.ts through execution-engine.ts args parsing.
acceptanceCriteria: execution-engine.ts accepts --reasoning-effort <value> CLI arg parsed alongside existing --thinking-enabled and --thinking-budget
spawnClaude() appends --thinking flag when reasoning.enabled is true and --effort <value> when effort is specified
Pipeline trigger payload Zod schema in pipeline.ts adds reasoningEffort as optional string field
worker.ts passes reasoningEffort from job payload to execution-engine.ts as --reasoning-effort arg
Existing --thinking-enabled and --thinking-budget args continue to work unchanged (backward compat)
npx tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors

userStories.title: OpenCode reasoning pass-through in execution-engine.ts
userStories.description: Extend spawnOpenCode() in execution-engine.ts to pass reasoning config to the OpenCode CLI when using a reasoning-capable model. OpenCode accepts provider-specific params via environment or config.
acceptanceCriteria: spawnOpenCode() checks if the model has reasoning capability via detectCapability(model) before injecting reasoning params
When reasoning is enabled and model is effort-levels type, OPENCODE_REASONING_EFFORT env var is set in the child process environment
When reasoning is enabled and model is anthropic-thinking type, OPENCODE_THINKING_BUDGET env var is set
When reasoning is disabled or model has reasoningType: 'none', no extra env vars are injected
Execution-engine integration test asserts env vars are present/absent based on reasoning config
npx tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors

userStories.title: Reasoning config stored in spec JSON and read on pipeline trigger
userStories.description: Persist reasoning config in the spec JSON file when a spec is generated or updated, and read it back when the pipeline trigger defaults are applied. The spec's reasoning config serves as the default for new runs.
acceptanceCriteria: POST /api/specs/generate accepts optional reasoning: { enabled, effort } in request body and writes it to the spec JSON file
Spec JSON files written with top-level reasoning field alongside model field
GET /api/specs/:id returns reasoning field in the spec object
POST /api/pipeline/trigger uses spec JSON reasoning as default when no explicit reasoning params provided in request body
Explicit reasoning params in trigger request override spec JSON defaults
Jest test: generate spec with reasoning config, then trigger pipeline, assert job payload contains correct reasoning values

userStories.title: Reasoning controls in SpecsPanel.tsx Forge brief flow
userStories.description: Add a Reasoning Mode section to the Forge brief Advanced Options panel in SpecsPanel.tsx. Controls are dynamically rendered based on the selected model's reasoningCapability. Preferences are persisted per-model in localStorage.
acceptanceCriteria: Reasoning Mode section is hidden when selected model has supportsReasoning: false
When supportsReasoning is true and effortLevels exists, a segmented control renders the exact effort levels from the capability object (not hardcoded)
Enable/disable toggle allows turning reasoning off even when the model supports it
Per-model preferences saved to localStorage key rorca:reasoning:<modelId> and restored when same model is re-selected
When model changes, controls update to reflect the new model's capability with its saved preferences
Reasoning config is included in the POST /api/specs/generate request body

userStories.title: Reasoning badge and controls in SpecModelControlBar.tsx
userStories.description: Display a reasoning badge on SpecModelControlBar when the spec was generated with reasoning enabled, and allow changing reasoning config before running the spec in the pipeline.
acceptanceCriteria: When spec.reasoning.enabled is true, a badge showing the reasoning type and effort level renders in SpecModelControlBar (e.g. 'Reasoning: high')
Badge is hidden when spec.reasoning is undefined or enabled is false
A popover or inline control allows changing reasoning config before triggering a run, with controls driven by the model's reasoningCapability
Changed reasoning config is passed to POST /api/pipeline/trigger as override (does not mutate spec JSON)
Badge uses a distinct icon (brain/sparkle) to visually differentiate from model badge

userStories.title: Reasoning defaults table in Settings > Model & Providers
userStories.description: Add a per-model reasoning defaults table to the Settings > Model & Providers tab. Users can set default effort level, toggle global auto-enable, and force override per model.
acceptanceCriteria: Settings > Model & Providers tab renders a Reasoning Defaults section showing all installed/recently used models
Each row shows: model name, supportsReasoning badge, default effort dropdown (populated from effortLevels), force-on/force-off/auto radio
Global toggle 'Always enable reasoning for capable models' sets default for all models without individual overrides
Settings saved to GET/PUT /api/settings/display or a new dedicated endpoint and persisted in user_settings DB row
On page load, saved defaults are fetched and pre-populate the table
npx tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors

userStories.title: Cost multiplier display in Forge brief and dry-run
userStories.description: Show estimated cost impact when reasoning is enabled in the Forge brief flow and dry-run preview. Use the costMultiplier from ReasoningCapability to compute relative cost.
acceptanceCriteria: When reasoning is toggled on in Forge brief, a cost impact label renders: e.g. '~2x base cost' using costMultiplier[effort]
When costMultiplier is undefined for the model, label shows 'Cost impact unknown'
Dry-run response from POST /api/pipeline/trigger?dryRun=true includes a reasoningCostMultiplier field
Dry-run UI preview panel shows 'Base cost' and 'With reasoning (Nx)' line items when reasoning is enabled
Cost display updates reactively when effort level changes in the segmented control

userStories.title: FinOps dashboard: reasoning tokens breakdown
userStories.description: Extend the FinOps analytics panel to break out reasoning/thinking tokens separately from regular tokens where providers report them. Add a reasoning tokens column to the token usage table and chart.
acceptanceCriteria: token_usage table row includes reasoning_tokens INTEGER column (migration 20260403XXXXXX_add_reasoning_tokens.sql)

chatComplete() extracts reasoning token count from provider response (Anthropic usage.cache_read_input_tokens proxy or thinking block token count; OpenAI usage.completion_tokens_details.reasoning_tokens) and stores in token_usage
Analytics panel token usage table shows Reasoning Tokens column (hidden when all zero)
Stacked bar chart in FinOps separates 'Thinking' from 'Output' token segments
Migration uses timestamp format, guards with IF NOT EXISTS

userStories.title: Reasoning model highlighting in model selector dropdown
userStories.description: Add visual indicators for reasoning-capable models in all model picker dropdowns across the UI. Group reasoning models or show a distinct icon. Show supported effort levels in the model details tooltip.
acceptanceCriteria: Model selector dropdown (ModelPickerPopover.tsx or equivalent) renders a brain/sparkle icon next to model names with supportsReasoning: true
Tooltip on hover shows supported effort levels: e.g. 'Supports: low, medium, high reasoning effort'
A filter chip 'Reasoning' filters the dropdown to show only reasoning-capable models
OpenRouter section in model picker uses the reasoningCapability from the enriched fetchOpenRouterModels response
Non-reasoning models show no icon and are not affected by the Reasoning filter chip
npx tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors

userStories.title: rorca_model_capabilities MCP tool
userStories.description: Add a new MCP tool rorca_model_capabilities that returns the computed ReasoningCapability for a given model ID. Update rorca_generate_spec and rorca_pipeline_trigger to accept reasoning config.
acceptanceCriteria: rorca_model_capabilities tool registered in backend/src/mcp/server.ts with input schema: { modelId: string }
Tool calls detectCapability(modelId) and returns the full ReasoningCapability object as JSON
rorca_generate_spec tool accepts optional reasoning: { enabled, effort } parameter in addition to existing thinkingEnabled/thinkingBudget
Old thinkingEnabled/thinkingBudget params on rorca_generate_spec are still accepted and mapped to reasoning config (backward compat)
rorca_pipeline_trigger accepts optional reasoningEffort string parameter
npx tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors

userStories.title: Graceful degradation: retry without reasoning on provider error
userStories.description: Implement the retry-without-reasoning fallback in chatComplete(). If a provider returns an error when reasoning params are included, catch it, retry the same request without reasoning, log a warning, and update an in-memory capability cache to mark the model as non-reasoning for this session.
acceptanceCriteria: chatComplete() catches provider errors containing 'reasoning' or 'thinking' in the error message and retries once without reasoning params
On retry success, logs a structured warning: { model, error, action: 'retried_without_reasoning' }
An in-memory Map<string, ReasoningCapability> capability override cache is updated with supportsReasoning: false for the offending model
Subsequent calls for the same model in the same process skip reasoning params without retrying
Jest test mocks provider to throw on first call with reasoning, asserts second call omits reasoning params and returns successfully
Cache does not persist across process restarts (in-memory only)

userStories.title: Auto-suggest reasoning based on spec complexity
userStories.description: Implement the 'Auto' effort option that analyzes spec complexity (story count, dependency depth, domain keywords) and suggests an appropriate reasoning effort level. Show an auto-suggestion banner in Forge brief.
acceptanceCriteria: computeAutoEffort(stories: UserStory[]): { effort: string, rationale: string } function in reasoning-detector.ts returns 'high' for >20 stories or max dependency depth >3, 'medium' for 10-20 stories, 'low' otherwise
Forge brief Reasoning Mode section includes an 'Auto' chip in the effort segmented control
When 'Auto' is selected, the system computes effort after brief is entered and shows a rationale banner: 'This 30-story spec is complex. Reasoning: high recommended. ~4x base cost'
Auto-computed effort is sent in the generate request as the effective effort value
Selecting a manual effort level deselects Auto
Auto-suggestion only appears for models with supportsReasoning: true

userStories.title: Reasoning config in TriggerPopover.tsx run action
userStories.description: Extend TriggerPopover.tsx to show reasoning config controls when the spec's model supports reasoning. Allow overriding effort level per-run without mutating the spec JSON.
acceptanceCriteria: TriggerPopover fetches the spec model's reasoningCapability via GET /api/config/model-capability?modelId=<model> or from the enriched model list
When supportsReasoning is true, a collapsible Reasoning section renders in the popover with effort segmented control
Default value pre-populated from spec.reasoning or model default from settings
Selected reasoning config passed in POST /api/pipeline/trigger body as reasoningEffort and thinkingEnabled fields
When model has reasoningType: 'none', the Reasoning section is hidden entirely
npx tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors

userStories.title: GET /api/config/model-capability endpoint and capability cache
userStories.description: Add a REST endpoint GET /api/config/model-capability?modelId=<id> that returns ReasoningCapability for any model ID. Back it with a TTL cache (5 min) to avoid repeated OpenRouter API calls. Wire it to the capability override cache from graceful degradation.
acceptanceCriteria: GET /api/config/model-capability?modelId=<id> returns 200 with ReasoningCapability JSON for any model ID
For OpenRouter models, makes a single OpenRouter API call to fetch model metadata (or uses cached fetchOpenRouterModels result), then calls detectCapability
For non-OpenRouter models (anthropic/, openai/ prefix), returns capability from pattern-matching only (no external API call)
Response is cached in-memory for 5 minutes per modelId to avoid redundant OpenRouter calls
If modelId is missing from query, returns 400 ValidationError
JSDoc @swagger annotation present on the route
npx tsc --noEmit passes with zero errors
